analysis.investment_thesis: Affle 3i is the closest thing to a textbook Fisher growth stock in this set: a technology-driven mobile advertising platform compounding revenues at 45% CAGR over seven years, generating consistently positive free cash flow (INR 266 Cr in FY25), and systematically expanding its global footprint through targeted acquisitions of programmatic ad-tech platforms. The debt-free balance sheet (INR 1,047 Cr cash, D/E 0.01) gives it the financial freedom to compound organically and acquisitively.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 45.1% over seven years is exceptional and absolute revenue growth is accelerating (INR 1,434→1,843→2,266 Cr over FY23–FY25) — this is not deceleration in percentage terms masking slower absolute gains
Consistent positive FCF across all five tracked years (FY25: INR 266 Cr), which is rare among high-growth Indian tech companies — the business funds its own growth without chronic dilution

Global ad-tech platform assembled via acquisitions (Appnext, MediaSmart, Jampp, RevX, YouAppi) across app discovery, programmatic display, and mobile retargeting — genuine platform diversification across channels and geographies
key_risks: ROE of 14.0% and ROCE of 16.8% are below Fisher's 20% benchmarks — the large intangible/goodwill base from acquisitions suppresses measured returns on equity

Operating margin of 18.1% is decent but below what Fisher would expect from a pure software/platform business — gross margin of 29.1% suggests significant traffic acquisition costs that cap margin expansion
Google and Meta control 60%+ of global digital ad spend; Affle's programmatic platforms must continuously differentiate on performance ROI to retain advertiser budgets
red_flags: Investing CF of -INR 572 Cr in FY24 driven by acquisitions — each acquisition resets the goodwill clock and integration risk must be monitored for signs of cultural or technology dilution
The company's 'other income' line (INR 94 Cr in FY25, up from INR 42 Cr in FY21) is growing and includes returns on cash investments — without it, operating profit growth would look modestly weaker
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Affle's core proposition — cost-per-converted-user (CPCU) mobile advertising that charges advertisers only for verified app installs or transactions — is a differentiated performance model that aligns incentives with outcomes. This is the kind of innovation-led, customer-value-centric business Fisher's scuttlebutt would unearth as having a sticky and growing client base. The India mobile advertising market is underpenetrated (sub-40% smartphone internet penetration in rural India), and Affle's international expansion through acquisitions in Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Latin America extends the runway significantly. Revenue growth at 45% CAGR over seven years with zero meaningful debt is genuinely rare.

The key Fisher question is whether management can integrate and scale the acquired platforms without destroying unit economics. The FY25 OCF of INR 426 Cr (vs INR 262 Cr in FY24) and FCF of INR 266 Cr (vs INR 147 Cr in FY24) suggest the integration is working and profitability is improving rather than eroding. At P/E 47x and forward P/E 35x, the stock prices in continued execution — but for a 40%+ compounding business with net cash and positive FCF, Fisher would view this as a reasonable price for an exceptional company.
